subject: West Medford Community Center Black History Program
overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted its monthly 'First Fridays' event celebrating Black History Month with a featured interview and a musical performance. The program focused on the center's leadership transition, future civic initiatives, and a historical survey of African American music.

items.title: Program Opening and Guest Update
items.summary: Terry Carter opened the 2023 First Fridays series and announced that the scheduled guest, NAACP President Jillian Harvey, would be rescheduled for March due to illness.

items.title: Interview with Executive Director Lisa Crossman
items.summary: Executive Director Lisa Crossman discussed her professional background, her transition from board member to director, and the challenges of managing the center following the pandemic.

items.title: WMCC Strategic Vision and Resiliency Hub
items.summary: Crossman detailed her vision for the center, including financial independence, the establishment of a teen space, and participation in the city's Resiliency Hub for flood preparedness.

items.title: Civic Engagement and Community Collaboration
items.summary: The discussion highlighted the importance of partnerships and the center's role as a repository for African American history and culture in Medford.

items.title: Call to Civic Action
items.summary: Crossman urged residents to become more involved in local government by applying for city commissions and participating in policy-making processes.

items.title: Community Announcements
items.summary: Carter announced upcoming events including senior lunch programs, a Black Entrepreneurs Marketplace on February 18, and a teen comedy workshop during school vacation week.

items.title: Musical History Performance
items.summary: Katani Sumner and Mark Copeland III performed a 'musical history tour' tracing the evolution of African American music from spirituals and blues to jazz, gospel, and hip-hop.
